key_insight: STAR-XPC predicts X-ray transmission through polymer composites in milliseconds, closely matching computationally expensive Monte Carlo simulations.
engineering_relevance: The model could accelerate screening of polyethylene-based radiation shields across composition, thickness, and X-ray source settings.
method: Embed molecular constituents with pretrained ChemBERTa.
Combine constituent embeddings, mass fractions, and four bulk physical descriptors.
Use a permutation-invariant Set Transformer supporting up to 11 constituents to predict I(t)/I₀.
evidence_signal: On 4,697 simulated configurations, leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation achieved R² = 0.9988 and median absolute percentage error of 1.15%.
watch_item: Performance beyond the simulated polyethylene-based composites, 0.15–2.5 mm thickness range, and four tested tube voltages remains unestablished.
paper_title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
